annotations.title: Compacted GEMM1 still spends 88.4% of wave time in WAIT
annotations.note: The deterministic route scan changes the output layout but not the GEMM1 feed bottleneck. The four waves average 113.0k cycles, with 88.36% WAIT, 10.34% EXEC, and 1.28% STALL. There is still only one routed workgroup per CU.
annotations.suggestion: The remaining optimization target is the W1 payload pipeline or routed-expert work reduction. Stage-2 grouping has already removed the downstream duplicate traffic.

annotations.title: vmcnt(7) waits remain the dominant GEMM1 instruction cost
annotations.note: The largest wait blocks at idx 4369, 3308, 3923, and 3275 each accumulate 8.7-9.1k cycles across the four traced waves. Route compaction adds only a small scan; it does not change the four-role W1 load/MFMA schedule.
annotations.suggestion: Do not revisit the tested rolling-load forms: per-role rolling raised wave duration to 145.9k cycles, and next-batch overlap also regressed. A future pipeline needs asynchronous staging or a different W1 work decomposition.

annotations.title: Route scan adds about 7.3k cycles per traced wave
annotations.note: The compact-output wave averages 113.0k cycles versus 105.7k for route-private GEMM1. The scan uses two coalesced routed-ID reads, ballots, popcounts, and first-bit selection. Device-level Stage 1 remains near 61-62 us because the added work is small relative to the W1 waits.
annotations.suggestion: Keep the scan: it enables a roughly 2 us Stage-2 gain and improves numerical stability. Further scan tuning is lower priority than W1 traffic.

annotations.title: Compaction cannot remove GEMM1's 26.7% extra TCC requests
annotations.note: PMC records 3.429M TCC requests and 2.879M misses, essentially unchanged from route-private token-wave GEMM1 and still above forced f16in's 2.707M requests and 2.657M misses. Every routed W1 projection is still computed independently.
annotations.suggestion: Closing exact M=16 now requires grouping duplicate experts in GEMM1 or retaining sorted f16in as the fallback. Stage-2-only work cannot erase this traffic.
